From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Sam Park <sam.park@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Severe latency and errors on tenant acct-771 during morning spike

Marissa / Sam — initial triage: I pulled traces for the request IDs in the dump and see repeated long stalls in KV fetches followed by large batch retries. Pattern: tenant traffic causes oversized batching windows; KV misses cascade and hot-lane HOL blocking occurs while the runtime waits on a small subset of heavy keys. That matches the throughput collapse + increased 5xx (upstream timeouts).

Immediate mitigations I've pushed as short-lived actions (on the affected pool):
- Reduced max batch size from 256 -> 64 for tenant pool (temporary)
- Disabled aggressive prefix prefetch for acct-771 (to avoid polluting KV space)

Early results: p50 dropped to ~1.2s within 10m, p99 has moved to ~6s but still elevated. Error rate down from 7% -> 2.1%. These are emergency knobs; not a permanent config.

Next steps I recommend (short):
1) Stabilize with the smaller batch size and monitor for 1h.
2) Run a targeted KV rehash for victim keys (we have an index of hot keys in the dump) — this prevents eviction cycles.
3) Plan a removal of the aggressive cross-tenant prefetch policy for bursty tenants; prepare a canary.

I can execute the KV rehash with ops approval; estimated 18–30m work.

Jonas
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Sam Park <sam.park@acme.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Severe latency and errors on tenant acct-771 during morning spike

Adding context / suggested permanent changes:

Root cause hypothesis: misaligned flow-control and KV windowing. Our prefetch policy opens windows that allow a tenant with high variability to occupy the hot-lane; combined with large max batch sizes, a small set of hot keys stalls many requests (HOL). Prefetch also pollutes neighbor tenant slots causing eviction thrash.

Permanent mitigations I propose (trajectory plan):
- Introduce per-tenant adaptive window caps (max active prefixes) — start with a conservative cap for OLAP-like tenants.
- Add a KV admission control for prefetch: limit cross-tenant prefetch when pool load > 60%.
- Default batch max to 128 and allow per-tenant override tied to SLA tier.
- Ship a diagnostics flag that exports in-flight prefix list for every incident (helps faster RCA).

I attached a short rollout doc (proposed-kv-windowing-rollout.md) and a CSV snapshot of customer SLA thresholds (acme_q2_sla_snapshot.csv).

I'll prepare a canary for the window cap change and run it with Acme's test tenant tomorrow morning.

-Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Production impact: flow-control misalignment causing throughput collapse

Folks — quick executive update for Acme and our leadership:

What happened (short): an aggressive prefetch + large batch windows allowed a bursty tenant to occupy KV hot-lane, creating HOL blocking and eviction thrash across the pool. That produced high tail latency and ~7% 5xx for affected calls.

What we did (immediate):
- Emergency knobs: reduced max batch and disabled prefix prefetch for acct-771 — observed p50/p99 and error-rate improvements.
- Jonas completed a targeted KV rehash for hot keys; Rishi has proposed a set of permanent mitigations.

Next actions (30/60/90):
- 30m: Continue monitoring with current emergency settings (Jonas).
- 60m: Prepare a staged canary for per-tenant window capping; coordinate with Acme for low-traffic window tomorrow. (Rishi)
- 90d: Ship adaptive admission control and diagnostic exposure; include in release notes and update default batch cap. (Eng roadmap)

Acme — Laura will coordinate a short post-incident review and share slides for your execs. We will provide a timeline for the canary and the final rollout by end of day tomorrow.

Thank you for quick escalation and patience.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
